title: Chester to Flint Coastal Path Walking Route

images.title: The Dee Coastal Path at Saltney by Jeff Buck, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: The Dee Coastal Path at Saltney. The River Dee was canalised in 1737 to try and maintain a deep water channel through the salt marshes (Salt Ney) for trade into Chester. This must have been a partial success as industry was established along the banks of the river for many years, however, the channel eventually silted up and trade died. Nevertheless, in the recent past, Airbus Industries have started to use a shallow draft barge to move the huge A380 wings up river to Mostyn Docks for onward transportation by sea. The footbridge at Saltney Ferry is near here.

images.title: Gary Bealr, CC BY-SA 4.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Flint Castle

description: This walk takes you from Chester to Flint along a section of the Wales Coast Path. You'll follow the waymarked trail for just under 11 miles along flat footpaths. The first section takes you along the River Dee to Connah's Quay before finishing at the historic Flint Castle. Along the way there are excellent views across the Dee Estuary to the Wirral on the other side.You can continue your walking on theFlint to Prestatyn Coastal Path.
